<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Keep tensors derived from weights (kernel constants, inverse scales, decode copies) at their startup addresses when post-load processing reruns on a weight reload, so captured CUDA graphs read the new values instead of freed memory. Part of the direct weight reload work (RFC #54477, rule 3). Builds on #64357 (merged); replaces aoshen02/vllm#180.

> **Direct reload.** #64336 (direct reload core) is now in main, and this branch has main merged. The direct reload tests that waited on it are back in this PR (see Validation). Results marked "direct" were measured with #64336 on both arms, before it merged.

## Claims

- After a weight reload with CUDA graphs on, MoE models whose post-load step derives kernel tensors serve the same output as before the reload. Without this PR they collapse:
  - gpt-oss-20b (TRT-LLM MXFP4, direct reload): GSM8K 0.39 → 0.01;
  - Qwen3-30B-A3B-NVFP4 (CuteDSL): 0.90 → 0.01 with direct reload, 0.93 → 0.00 with layerwise reload.
- With direct reload (#64336), every tensor the MoE kernel reads keeps its cold-start address across a reload on these backends: TRT-LLM MXFP4/NVFP4, CuteDSL NVFP4 (including per-locality-domain shards), FlashInfer CUTLASS NVFP4/FP8, and per-tensor FP8 (including TRT-LLM FP8 per-tensor's shuffled weights).
- After a draft-model weight update, the tensors the V2 speculator's FULL CUDA graph reads (DFlash/DSpark context K/V weights and norms, including Beam's DFlash2 and Kimi-K3's DSpark drafters) keep their addresses. Without this PR, Beam DFlash2 acceptance fell from 7.03 to 4.89 after an update.
- The same holds for linear kernels that derive tensors in their post-load step (CUTLASS/Triton INT8 asymmetric `azp_adj`, CUTLASS W4A8, Marlin W4A8-INT8/FP8, b12x NVFP4 W4A16, ModelOpt block-quant), for the ROCm gpt-oss MXFP4 AITER shuffles, Kimi-K3 AMD `_w_fold` and the bf16x3 router split, and for MXFP4 MoE on Marlin (gpt-oss-20b GSM8K 0.43 → 0.00 after a reload without this PR, 0.45 → 0.43 with it).
- Humming MoE: its post-load step runs once per quant method; direct reload refuses it (in main with #64336).
- Across 17 served models with direct reload (3 full-checkpoint updates each, measured by aoshen02), GSM8K holds after every update with this PR; on main it collapses on 8 of them (e.g. gpt-oss-120b 0.80 → 0.006, Kimi-K3 0.95 → 0.25).
- No cold-start change: GSM8K, throughput and KV cache match the base on 12 model/backend configurations, all within noise.

## Validation

All runs are on GB200 with nightly `4b47db922` plus this branch's Python files. "Base" = main `255431b5e` + #64357 + #64336.

**Reload with CUDA graphs on.** Start a server on a checkpoint, then record greedy tokens and top-1 logprobs on 8 fixed prompts (one request at a time) and a 300-question GSM8K slice. Push 2 weight updates through the NCCL weight-transfer engine and record the same again. "Greedy = fresh" compares with a fresh server on the last checkpoint sent; for a same-weight update the fresh server is the one before the update.

| Model, MoE backend, reload mode | Update | Base: GSM8K pre → post, greedy = fresh | This PR: GSM8K pre → post, greedy = fresh |
|---|---|---|---|
| gpt-oss-20b, TRT-LLM MXFP4, direct | same weights ×2 | 0.390 → **0.013**, 0/8 | 0.393 → 0.413, **8/8** |
| gpt-oss-20b, TRT-LLM MXFP4, direct | 2 perturbed variants | → 0.007 (fresh 0.007), **0/8** | → 0.003 (fresh 0.003), **8/8** |
| Qwen3-30B-A3B-NVFP4, CuteDSL, direct | same weights ×2 | 0.903 → **0.007** | 0.927 → 0.900 |
| Qwen3-30B-A3B-NVFP4, CuteDSL, layerwise | same weights ×2 | 0.927 → **0.000** | 0.923 → 0.910 |
| Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8 (block), TRT-LLM FP8, direct and layerwise | same weights / perturbed | 8/8 | 8/8 |

- The "this PR" MXFP4/NVFP4 rows ran on `a4a859064`; the FP8 rows ran on this PR's first commit (`deaba72c6`). Since then the FP8 and MXFP4/NVFP4 paths changed only in comments and type annotations, and the direct-reload-only branch of `replace_parameter` moved to #64336.
- The perturbed variants flip the low bits of every FP4/FP8 payload and scale the scales by 2^k. These models score ≈0 themselves, so those rows are judged by token equality with the fresh server.
- One perturbed gpt-oss run (job 41424) gave 0/8 against the fresh server. This was not reproducible: three reruns gave 8/8.
- **NVFP4 CuteDSL** is not bit-reproducible across servers: two cold starts agree on 0–2 of 8 greedy sequences. GSM8K is its signal.
- **FP8 block quant** has no per-tensor derived constants, so it is a no-regression row.

**Served reload across models (aoshen02, [review](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/64692#issuecomment-6543567448)).** Direct reload, GSM8K before → after 3 full-checkpoint updates, main vs this PR plus the review commits (aoshen02/vllm#227, now on this branch). ## Details

**Root cause.** `process_weights_after_loading` reruns on every reload (#64357), in both layerwise and direct mode. Many quant methods and models build tensors from the weights there as new allocations: kernel constants (SwiGLU alpha/beta/clamp folded by `g1_alphas`, `g1_scale_c`, inverse activation scales), experts objects rebuilt with fresh constants, decode-path copies. Captured CUDA graphs keep the startup pointers, so after a reload they read freed memory. Every weight is reloaded correctly, so comparing weight values cannot see it.

**Fix.**
- `replace_parameter` already refills parameters in place (unchanged here).
- `refill_derived(obj, name, tensor)` (new) refills a plain attribute in place when shape, dtype and device match, else replaces it. It never creates a parameter, and the held tensor must own its storage.
- MoE experts objects list the tensors their kernels read in `kept_constants`. `keep_constants(layer)` keeps them on the layer and points the new object at them. `FallbackExperts` forwards it to both wrapped experts.

<details>
<summary>Sites</summary>

- **MoE:**
  - TRT-LLM MXFP4/FP8/NVFP4 constants, including the MXFP4 LoRA experts (which declare the MXFP4 names themselves, since the MRO resolves the base experts' empty tuple first) and their FC1 bias index, now built at construction instead of lazily (Quark NVFP4 skips the experts' post-load step and keeps the constructor's).
  - FlashInfer CUTLASS SwiGLU constants, and `fake_input_scale` on its MXFP4-weight / MXFP8-activation path.
  - CuteDSL `per_token_global_scale` and per-locality-domain shards.
  - CUTLASS FP8/W4A8 strides.
  - TRT-LLM FP8 per-tensor: the weight shuffle writes into the weights instead of rebinding `.data` (without alignment padding `w2` is the layer parameter itself).
  - FP8 per-tensor `g1/g2_alphas` and `a1/a2_gscale` (now also Quark W8A8 FP8).
  - NVFP4 `a1/a2_gscale`; compressed-tensors NVFP4 input scales.
- **Linear kernels:** CUTLASS/Triton INT8 asymmetric `azp_adj`, CUTLASS W4A8 `weight_chan_scale` and Marlin W4A8-INT8 `input_global_scale` (linear and compressed-tensors WNA16 MoE) go through `replace_parameter`; Marlin W4A8-FP8 scales its weight scales in place; b12x NVFP4 W4A16 and ModelOpt block-quant reuse the packed weight's storage, as b12x MXFP8 and tensor FP8 already do.
- **MXFP4 MoE on Marlin:** `begin_direct_reload` zeroes the storage it views back to checkpoint layout, since the loaders write only the unpadded region and the repack moved bytes into the padding. A stopgap: #64352 records and fills the padding right before the post-load step, which also covers layerwise reload and is what the load plan (#64418) needs.
- **ROCm:** the gpt-oss MXFP4 AITER CK shuffles (`AITER_MXFP4_BF16`, `AITER_MXFP4_MXFP4`) return the shuffled tensors for `replace_parameter` instead of rebinding `.data`; Kimi-K3 AMD `_w_fold` and `GateLinear._bf16x3_weight` use `refill_derived`.
- **Fused MoE gate:** with fused shared experts (e.g. ROCm AITER), Qwen3-Next/Qwen3.5 and AliceAI pass `shared_expert_gate` to `MoERunner`, which concatenated it with the router weight on the first forward and never rebuilt it, so routing kept the cold-start gates. `finalize_model_weights` now refills `_combined_gate_weight` in place after every load (`test_fused_gate_weight_refilled_after_reload`: fails on the previous head, passes with the fix; slurm 43121 / 43118).
- **Kimi-K3:** the specialized decode's packed MoE front, padded TP16 down projection, and KDA conv weight and norm, refreshed from a model-level post-load hook. The MLA inverse q/k scales. `PreparedMla` keeps the softmax and KV-cache scales as host floats; that is safe because no quant config gives K3's attention a KV-cache method, so its post-load step resets the q/k scales to 1.0 every run (a code comment says so).
- **GLM-5-next:** the indexer's fp32 head gate.
- **ModelOpt W4A16 NVFP4:** the gather copies (Qwen3-DSpark `markov_w2`), now refilled attributes instead of non-persistent buffers re-registered on every rerun.
- **Muse Spark:**
  - The residual alpha/beta coefficients and the NVIDIA NVFP4 MoE constants.
  - The router output multiplier, two patterns:
    - NVIDIA folds it in the router weight's loader (once per load).
    - AMD already keeps its post-load fold on main, guarded by a flag the loader clears, with its bf16x3 router planes refilled in place; unchanged here.
- **Drafters:** DFlash/DSpark context K/V weights and norm stacks (Qwen3, Laguna, Gemma4, Muse, Beam DFlash2, Kimi-K3 DSpark), Gemma4 MTP's gathered lm_head (built in the post-load step, outside inference mode), LiLiCorr buffers. Drafter weights are updated through the weight-transfer engines' draft target (`start_draft_weight_update`), whose finish reruns the drafter's post-load step.

</details>

**Limitations / known gaps.** Direct reload (#64336) is the target path; layerwise reload is planned for removal (F10 in the #54477 tracker), so its gaps are listed but not planned for fixing.

*Affect direct reload:*
- **Muse Spark MegaMoE:** `finalize_weights` returns early once transformed and drops checkpoint parameters, so a reload leaves the experts stale (or fails to load them), along with the hybrid TRT-LLM scales built there. Same on main. Tracked as F15.
- **DeepGEMM NVFP4 MegaMoE (MiniMax-M3 NVFP4, Step-5 NVIDIA): the L2 activation scale is a host float.** The max of `w2_input_scale` is passed by value to the Triton prepare kernel and to DeepGEMM `nvfp4_mega_moe`, so CUDA graphs keep the cold-start value when an update changes `w2_input_scale` (QAT-style updates such as verl's NVFP4 W4A4 send it on every sync). Fix: vllm-project/DeepGEMM#49 takes the scale as a device tensor, then vLLM bumps the pin and passes a buffer refilled in place. Tracked as F16; moving the max into PWAL is #64418 L2.
- **Qwen3 XPress:** `XPressHead.build_fused_buffers` builds its fused copies anew.
- **FlashInfer b12x NVFP4 MoE** (SM12x only, opt-in): it rebinds the weight scales to new storage and rebuilds their MMA views and `_fc2_input_scale`.
- **FlashInfer MoE-EP megakernel** rebinds the layer parameters to new adapter buffers on every rerun.
- **DeepSeek-V4 AMD:** e8m0 upcasts, compressor `cat` and the MegaMoE early return; handled separately in aoshen02/vllm#226. None of them runs for V4.1.
- **Qwen3-30B-A3B-NVFP4 CuteDSL output is not reproducible within one server, reload or not,** so `test_reload_keeps_moe_output` checks only its tensor addresses (gpt-oss TRT-LLM keeps the output comparison too). The token comparison failed about 1 in 10 CI runs. On GB200 (slurm 41919), generating the same 4 prompts 20 times on one server without any reload, every repeat differed in tokens from the first and 6 of 20 failed `check_logprobs_close` (1 of 20 eager); after each of 10 reloads, 3 of 10 failed (1 of 10 eager), at the same rate. Top logprobs moved by ~0.2 between repeats. None of the 3225 GPU tensors reachable from the model (parameters, buffers and plain attributes, including quant methods, MoE kernels and experts) moved across any of the 10 reloads.
- **Untested in CI:** the Gemma4 MTP, DSpark (Muse, Gemma4, Kimi-K3), Beam DFlash2 and LiLiCorr drafter refills (the CI test covers Qwen3 DFlash), the Muse Spark NVIDIA router fold and NVFP4 MoE constants, the Kimi-K3 specialized decode `refresh_weights` (`decode.py`, `dense.py`, `kda/prepared.py`; validated end to end above) and the ROCm fixes (validated on MI355X above). Muse Spark is the only served row not rerun on the final code (the gated checkpoint is no longer accessible); it passed on the tree before the final simplification commit.

*Found in review, also on main ([aoshen02](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/64692#issuecomment-6550731296)):*
- **Compressed-tensors static per-tensor FP8 MoE** fails the first update with `input_scales of w1 and w3 of a layer must be equal`: the loader compares against the post-processed cold-start value. Dropping the check is #64418 L4.
- **`pack_tensors` does not align entries,** so `unpack_tensor` fails with `storage_offset() must be divisible by 8 to view Byte as Long` when a tensor follows one whose byte size is not a multiple of its element size (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, Mistral-Large-3, Inkling-NVFP4, Laguna).
- **Gemma-4 MTP draft update** fails with a size mismatch: after cold start the assistant's `embed_tokens` is the target's (see Validation).
- **LiLiCorr `load_weights`** checks full checkpoint coverage on every call; the packed engine calls it once per buffer, so drafts over one buffer fail with `checkpoint coverage mismatch`.
- **CUTLASS INT8 fails at engine startup on SM103** (`cutlass_gemm_caller ... Error Internal`), with or without this PR.

*Layerwise reload only (not planned):*
- **Laguna DFlash and LiLiCorr** build their buffers in `load_weights`, which meets meta tensors under per-tensor layerwise reload.
- **MoE quant configs are rebuilt around layerwise's temporary parameters.** Values stay correct, but the temporaries stay alive (F12).
- **Humming MoE** keeps its once-per-method guard; direct reload refuses it at cold start (in main, #64336).
- **Qwen3-30B-A3B-NVFP4 CuteDSL, layerwise reload: output after reloading the same weights is flaky.** It differed from the output before the reload in 2 of 4 GB200 runs (first token changed, coherent text). The direct reload case passed every run. The flakiness is not from the main merge: the layerwise case alone passed on both the pre-merge and post-merge heads. Without this PR, layerwise output collapses on every run (GSM8K 0.93 → 0.00). The case was removed from `test_reload_keeps_moe_output`.

The DFlash MXFP8 context K/V projection, listed here before, is fixed in #64357. MXFP4 MoE on Marlin, the ROCm paths above, Kimi-K3 `PreparedMla` and the linear kernels' rebuilt tensors, listed here before, are fixed or shown safe by aoshen02's follow-up commits (see Sites).

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Reloading the same weights must not change what a served MoE model
+generates: post-load processing reruns, and the tensors it derives for the
+kernels must stay where the captured CUDA graphs read them."""
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from tests.models.utils import check_logprobs_close
+from vllm.platforms import current_platform
+
+PROMPTS = [
+    "The capital of France is",
+    "List the first ten prime numbers:",
+    "Explain why the sky is blue in two sentences.",
+    "Q: A train travels 60 km in 45 minutes. What is its speed in km/h?\nA:",
+]
+
+
+def _gpu_tensor_ptrs(obj: object, path: str, ptrs: dict, seen: set) -> None:
+    """Record the address of every GPU tensor reachable from ``obj`` through
+    containers and attributes of vLLM objects, such as quant methods, MoE
+    kernels and experts."""
+    if isinstance(obj, torch.Tensor):
+        if obj.is_cuda:
+            ptrs[path] = obj.data_ptr()
+        return
+    if id(obj) in seen:
+        return
+    seen.add(id(obj))
+    if isinstance(obj, torch.nn.Module):
+        items = {**vars(obj), **obj._parameters, **obj._buffers, **obj._modules}
+    elif isinstance(obj, dict):
+        items = dict(obj)
+    elif isinstance(obj, (list, tuple)):
+        items = dict(enumerate(obj))
+    elif type(obj).__module__.startswith("vllm."):
+        items = dict(getattr(obj, "__dict__", {}))
+    else:
+        return
+    for name, value in items.items():
+        _gpu_tensor_ptrs(value, f"{path}.{name}", ptrs, seen)
+
+
+def _model_tensor_ptrs(worker) -> dict[str, int]:
+    ptrs: dict[str, int] = {}
+    _gpu_tensor_ptrs(worker.model_runner.model, "model", ptrs, set())
+    return ptrs
+
+

+    monkeypatch.setenv("VLLM_RELOAD_MODE", "direct")
+    monkeypatch.setenv("VLLM_ALLOW_INSECURE_SERIALIZATION", "1")
+    with vllm_runner(
+        model,
+        max_model_len=1024,
+        max_num_seqs=4,
+        enable_prefix_caching=False,
+        kernel_config={"enable_jit_warmup": False, "moe_backend": moe_backend},
+    ) as llm:
+        before = llm.generate_greedy_logprobs(PROMPTS, max_tokens=32, num_logprobs=5)
+        ptrs = llm.collective_rpc(_model_tensor_ptrs)
+        llm.collective_rpc("reload_weights")  # the served checkpoint
+        after_ptrs = llm.collective_rpc(_model_tensor_ptrs)
+        after = llm.generate_greedy_logprobs(PROMPTS, max_tokens=32, num_logprobs=5)
+    moved = [
+        sorted(n for n, p in old.items() if new.get(n) != p)
+        for old, new in zip(ptrs, after_ptrs)

## Review findings / changes

1. **Restored the direct-reload tests** that this PR handed to #64336, which merged without them: `test_direct_reload_keeps_kernel_tensor_addresses` (+ a new `fp8-static-trtllm` case), the direct cases of `test_reload_keeps_moe_output`, and `test_draft_weight_update_keeps_draft_tensor_addresses` for both modes. The humming refusal test is not restored (main's `test_direct_reload.py` covers it).
2. **Two more in-place refills** missed by the PR (full-tree audit):
   - FlashInfer TRT-LLM FP8 per-tensor MoE: `rotate_weights_for_fi_trtllm_fp8_per_tensor_moe` rebound `.data`; without alignment padding `w2` is `layer.w2_weight`, so its address moved on every rerun. Now `copy_`.

3. **Simplify**: `replace_parameter` keeps main's signature; dropped the `refill_derived` parameter assert, comments restating helpers, an incidental `gemma4_dspark` rewrite and a duplicate `test_utils` row. `keep_constants` mechanism unchanged.

## Unit / e2e tests (GB300)

issue_comments.body:
Follow-up to my previous comment: e2e coverage of every model and path this PR touches, run on the **final** review tree.

**Setup.** main = `b5755c3ba5`; PR = this branch + the review delta at `8b3f6b6c0f` (aoshen02/vllm#227); the two arms differ only in the PR's 47 files. `VLLM_RELOAD_MODE=direct`, 3 full-checkpoint updates over NCCL (target, then draft where there is one), nothing excluded except DSv4.1 Engram embedding tables. GB300 (NV, verda) and H200; nightly `2b009fc6d1` image (draft runs: `edad8b03c5`) + Python overlay. **Verdict** = GSM8K pre → post, plus spec-decode acceptance pre → post for draft models. Largest drop on the PR is -1.7 pt (gpt-oss-20b), against -0.7 to -0.9 pt on main on the MXFP4 rows.

**2. `pack_tensors` doesn't align entries.** Verified on the current head `e21ca26e22`, nightly `2b009fc6d1`:

Our harness took the receiver-side route instead: `unpack_tensor` clones a slice whose offset is misaligned.

**4. Gemma-4 MTP: a draft update fails** (jobs 21594/21595, both arms). TP2 is the configuration we ran; TP1 was not tried.

The cause: after cold start, the assistant's `model.embed_tokens` is replaced by the target's 3840-wide embedding, but the update still delivers the checkpoint's 262144×1024 `model.embed_tokens.weight`. That tensor's live, tied home is the draft `lm_head`.

**5. LiLiCorr: a draft update fails whenever the draft spans more than one packed buffer** (jobs 21694/21695 and 21708/21709, both arms).

Kimi-K3 specialized decode, previously listed as not covered: it now runs on both arms, and the PR holds on both pairs.

**Why it failed to cold start before.** The specialized MLA decode needs an FP8 KV cache; the default (`auto`) is BF16. `cutedsl/mla/dcp.py` `stock_decode` reads each cache row as FP8 and splits it at byte 512. A BF16 row is 1152 bytes, so the rope part comes out 640 wide instead of 64, which is the `Mismatched c_rope.shape[2]` error. `specialized_decode/runtime/__init__.py` `unsupported()` doesn't check the KV dtype, so it fails late with that error rather than a clear message. --attention-config '{"use_prefill_query_quantization":true,"mla_prefill_backend":"TRTLLM_RAGGED"}' \
```
--additional-config '{"decode_backend":"latency_specialized"}'
```
